summary:
All nine acceptance criteria hold. The strongest contact was the freshly published Release single-file exe run against real system data. The row under test was only ever reached through the injected failpoint, never through a failure Windows itself produced.

The listing failpoint in DirectoryReader.List sits where the design needs it. It replaces the result of a call that returned a page, after io.Query and before the `error != 0` check. LastCallAborted comes from the real call, so the pages already read are kept. FolderDone (Scanner.cs:275-285) then appends the children and flags the folder Unreadable, unchanged. This discharges O-009.

What I re-ran myself:
- Release publish: the exe was written now. The bundle contains FailListingOf and holds no "FSA_HOOK" string in ASCII or UTF-16.
- Core.Tests: 414/414.
- Fitness: 63/63 rules hold. rules-parity: AGREE.
- T-007: P kept 355 of 2,000 files and reads 'could not be read in full'. Q is read in full. R reads 'could not be opened'. Root = 9,646,080.
- T-008: 4 bad values, each exits 0xE0434352 with no report.
- Full `WindowCases.ps1 -Case All`: 48 passed in 652 s. N-001..N-004 not run.
- Both new mutants were caught by T-007.

My own driver, against the shipped exe:
- Criterion 9 on a fixture: with FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING set and no DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS, the scan equals the no-variable baseline (2,050 files, 8,396,800 bytes, no unreadable folder). The armed hook control on the same tree gives 405 files and 1 unreadable folder, so the fixture does span two pages.
- Criterion 9 on real C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore: 3,619 files and 921 folders with and without the variable. bytesOnDisk was identical; bytes differed by 2,232 from live data changing between runs. The armed hook control on FileRepository (1,001 entries) gives 1,813 files, 361 folders and 1 unreadable folder.
- O-017's four unfed values: all are refused at runtime.

O-017 is still open and owed to build-slice. T-008's $bad table (WindowCases.ps1:3046-3051) still feeds only 4 values. The empty-name, path-separator, error-18 and non-numeric-error refusals work, but nothing in the tree guards against a regression in them. The empty-name refusal is in the design contract's own error cases.

No loop: one build attempt, one code review.

The bug report was only a title. I assumed what the build check, design and code review agreed on: the Core scanner-level test already exists (TopLevelRowTextTests), and only the seam and the window case were owed.

checks.evidence: EXIT 0. The exe was written at 10:28:05, which was the current time (139,902,616 bytes). FailListingOf: 1 occurrence, ListingError: 1, FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING (ASCII): 0, FSA_HOOK (UTF-16): 0.
Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 414, Skipped: 0, Total: 414, Duration: 22 s

checks.what: Architecture rules, including SL-082's 'the shipped App can never arm the listing failpoint itself'
checks.evidence: 63 rule(s) checked against 116 parsed file(s). Every declared rule holds.
AGREE 12 facts <- 16 twinned entries, 29 patterns; 47 settled entries not compared. EXIT 0

checks.what: T-007: partial-read row beside a folder read in full and one denied outright
checks.evidence: The first log line is 'fail-listing armed p-… page 2 error 995', ahead of 'loaded mode=tree'. Exactly one 'fired p-… page 2'. Rows are Q, P, R. Q: no note, 2,000 children. P: 'could not be read in full', expander drawn and open, 355 of 2,000 kept, 355 children read and drawn (more than the 284.3 px viewport holds). R: 'could not be opened', no expander. Root = 9,646,080. Walked 359 rows, 0 unrendered. PASSED, EXIT 0, 6 s.

'folder1|2' gives FormatException, 'folder1|two|995' FormatException, 'folder1|1|995' ArgumentOutOfRangeException (page), 'folder1|2|0' ArgumentOutOfRangeException (win32Error). Each exits -532462766 (0xE0434352) with no report and the refusal as the only log line. PASSED, 20 s.

checks.what: Full window suite (criterion 8: existing cases unaffected)

checks.what: Mutant: Core member renamed so reflection finds nothing
checks.evidence: The hook logged 'fail-listing refused reason=MissingMethodException: the app has no FailListingOf(string, int, int, Action<string, int>) …'. Exit -532462766. T-007 failed on its first check only. Mutant PASSED (caught), EXIT 0.

checks.what: O-009: the failpoint sits upstream of the keep-earlier-pages and Unreadable logic (code reading)
checks.command: Read DirectoryReader.cs:87-131, SynchronousIoCancel.cs:278-297 and 327-360, Scanner.cs:140-160 and 270-285
checks.evidence: ListingError is applied right after io.Query returns and before `if (error != 0)`. It replaces only error==0, and only at the armed page. LastCallAborted is set in Exit() from the real call (false), so _count and _namesUsed are not reset. The earlier pages are kept, and FolderDone appends them, then AddFlags(Unreadable). The root goes through the path-less public List overload (Scanner.cs:203, 208), so it is never faulted.

checks.what: The worktree was not modified by validation; no stray processes or temp folders
checks.command: git status --porcelain=v1; Get-Process FsAnalyser.App; temp dir checks
checks.evidence: Only the pre-existing .taad/slices/SL-082 metadata changes. 0 FsAnalyser.App processes. My driver folder was deleted. 0 sl082-validate-* and 0 fsa-window-mutants scratch folders left.
They change this machine's SMB mappings, and none touch the listing failpoint or the tree's partial-read row. Not run, as in the build's and code review's runs.

checks.what: A partial listing failure produced by Windows itself (not injected)
checks.evidence: Spike 2 found local NTFS cannot produce one as an ordinary user. Spike 4 (SMB loopback) was never finished, and no engine stage runs it. Not attempted here.

criteria.criterion: 1. The listing failpoint is armed before the scan starts, when FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING is a well-formed value naming a folder present in the fixture
criteria.how: T-007 (re-run): 'fail-listing armed p-… page 2 error 995' is the first log line, ahead of 'loaded mode=tree', and it fired during the scan. Also seen in my fixture and DriverStore armed runs (armed line first, then loaded/sized, then fired).

criteria.criterion: 2. A bad FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING value (wrong arg count, non-numeric page, page<2, or a Core member reflection cannot find) is refused
criteria.how: T-008 feeds wrong arg count, non-numeric page, page 1 and error 0: each exits 0xE0434352 with no report and one refusal line. Missing member: the NoFailListingMember mutant (re-run) logs MissingMethodException and exits 0xE0434352. My driver also fed empty name, path separator, error 18 and non-numeric error, and all are refused. Those four are not in T-008 (O-017, open, owed to build-slice).

criteria.criterion: 3. A folder's listing fails partway when it spans at least 2 listing pages and the fault lands on page 2
criteria.how: T-007: 'fired p-… page 2'; P kept 355 of 2,000. My fixture control: pfold kept 355 of 2,000. Real data: DriverStore\FileRepository (1,001 entries) fired at page 2, giving 1,813/3,619 files and 1 unreadable folder.

criteria.criterion: 4. The tree row for a partially-read folder (0 < K < total listed before the fault)
criteria.how: T-007: P's drawn note is exactly 'could not be read in full', with an expander. childCount 355 (0<355<2000). Size and on-disk equal 355 × 4 KiB. Root = P + Q = 9,646,080.

criteria.criterion: 5. An unrelated sibling folder (Q), scanned in the same pass with no fault armed against it, is unaffected
criteria.how: T-007: Q is listed first and has P's multi-page shape. It has no note, an expander, and 2,000 children. The ListingFailsAnyFolder mutant (re-run) shows the check catches an unkeyed failpoint: Q drops to 355 with a note, and 'fired' shows two folders.

criteria.criterion: 6. A fully denied folder (R, via the existing ACL fixture route) sits next to the partial one
criteria.how: T-007: R reads 'could not be opened', no expander drawn, told apart from P's 'could not be read in full'.

criteria.criterion: 7. Expanding the partial row: the expander is opened before the report is captured
criteria.how: T-007 with WALK: P's container is expanded, and exactly 355 child rows are read and drawn, each by its own container, more than the 284 px viewport holds. This is a declared deviation: the evidence is tree mode's tree-row lines, not the schema-1 report. The row is opened programmatically through its container, not by a mouse or keyboard toggle on the glyph.

criteria.criterion: 8. The existing WindowCases.ps1 suite still passes after the schema-1 report change
criteria.how: No schema-1 change was made (a declared deviation; WindowReport.cs is untouched), so this holds trivially. Re-ran -Case All: all 46 existing cases plus T-007 and T-008 passed, EXIT 0. N-001..N-004 not run.

criteria.criterion: 9. The failpoint stays dormant outside the hook process: the Release single-file published exe run without DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS
criteria.how: Freshly published exe, variable set and no hook. On the fixture, results match the no-variable baseline (2,050 files, 8,396,800 bytes, no unreadable folder), and the armed control on the same tree gives 405 files and 1 unreadable, so the check is not vacuous. On real DriverStore, file/folder counts and bytesOnDisk are identical to the baseline with no unreadable folder; the armed control faults it. The bundle contains no 'FSA_HOOK' string, and the Fitness rule barring FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING and FailListingOf( in App holds.

obligations.evidence: Code: DirectoryReader.cs:109-124. SynchronousIoCancel.ListingError runs after io.Query returns and before the `error != 0` check. It replaces only a call that returned 0, at the armed page. LastCallAborted is set in Exit() from the real call, so it stays false, `_count` is not reset, and the earlier pages survive. Scanner.FolderDone (Scanner.cs:275-285) appends them, then flags Unreadable, unchanged. It sits one frame above OverrideQueryError (after Query's Settle rather than inside the guard); that is a declared deviation, and the effect downstream is the same as a Windows error on that call. Runtime: on the fixture the armed run kept 355 of pfold's 2,000 files and showed 'Unreadable folders (1)'. On real DriverStore, FileRepository was cut at page 2 (1,813 of 3,619 files) with 1 unreadable folder. T-007 shows the row's 'could not be read in full'.

Still open, owed to build-slice. The tree is unchanged: T-008's $bad table (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:3046-3051) holds only 'folder1|2', 'folder1|two|995', 'folder1|1|995' and 'folder1|2|0'. I fed the four missing values to the shipped exe with the hook. '|2|995' gives ArgumentException (Parameter 'folderName'). 'a\b|2|995' gives ArgumentException. 'folder1|2|18' gives ArgumentOutOfRangeException (Parameter 'win32Error'). 'folder1|2|x' gives FormatException. Each exits 0xE0434352 with no report. So the behaviour is correct today, but no test guards against a regression in it, including the design contract's own 'Empty name throws'.

not_reached: No listing ever failed partway because of Windows itself. The 'could not be read in full' row was reached only through the injected failpoint. Spike 2 showed local NTFS cannot produce one as an ordinary user, and spike 4 (SMB loopback) never ran its fault test. That a real mid-listing error, such as a share dropping between pages, takes the same path is inferred from code (the failpoint sits right after the query call), not observed.
The partial row's expander was opened by the hook's WALK through its container, not by a mouse or keyboard toggle on the drawn glyph.
N-001..N-004 (-IncludeNetwork) were not run. They change SMB mappings and do not touch this slice's row.
T-008's 0xE0434352 exit on a machine with WER's crash UI enabled: a dialog could hold the process until the 30 s timeout. Not reachable here, where every launch ended within about 0.1-1 s.
Only this machine's 1920x1080 display at 100% DPI (tree viewport 284 px). Other DPIs and screen sizes, and Windows 10, were not tried.
The failpoint has no disarm. Arming it from a parallel Core.Tests Fact was not exercised (nothing arms it there today).
